title: Pecan Tassies
headnote: From an old handwritten recipe card for pecan pie tarts; where it came from is not known. It makes 2 dozen: cream cheese pastry pressed into tiny muffin cups and filled with brown-sugar pecan filling.

items.raw: 1 package (3 ounces / 85 g) cream cheese, softened

steps.text: Beat the cream cheese and butter together until smooth. Add the flour and mix just until a soft dough forms. Wrap and chill at least 1 hour, until firm.
Heat the oven to 325°F. Divide the dough into 24 equal balls, about 1 tablespoon each. Press each into an ungreased mini muffin cup, pushing it evenly up the sides to the rim.
Whisk the egg, brown sugar, soft butter, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Divide half the pecans among the pastry cups. Spoon the filling over them, filling each cup about three-quarters full, then top with the remaining pecans.
Bake 25 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is puffed and set.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then run a thin knife around each one and lift it out. Cool completely on a rack.

notes.label: Don’t overfill
notes.text: the filling puffs as it bakes and glues the tassies to the pan if it runs over the rim.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: they keep a week in an airtight tin and freeze for 3 months.

notes.label: Variations
notes.text: swap walnuts for the pecans, or drop a few mini chocolate chips into each cup before filling.

openQuestion: Lyle’s list includes pecan tassies from Sue’s mom. Is this card hers, or is hers a different recipe? If different, please send it. The pecan amount on the card is faded — it looks like ⅔ cup.
